text:
erin: hi all, i'm running an onboarding workshop next week and need to confirm best practices for keys. we'll have ~12 attendees doing live streaming demos. can we do that with sandbox keys or should i request something else?
tom: welcome! :wave: sandbox usually can't handle 12 concurrent streams for long. For workshops we either: 1) request a short-lived hosted dev key with increased concurrency for the window, or 2) use recorded/playback streams so attendees don't hit the real API.
erin: thanks. if i request a hosted dev key, what's the process and lead time? also any privacy/audit concerns?
devex-bot: open the key request form: https://internal.redwood.devex/requests/keys. Choose "Workshop / Demo" and include: org/team, date/time window (UTC), expected concurrent streams, models, and whether participants will run code on their machines or in hosted labs. Typical turnaround 24-48h; mark as "urgent" in #devex for faster handling. Hosted dev keys are logged and can have restricted IPs and TTLs.
liam: for workshops we prefer per-attendee ephemeral tokens if you want them to run code locally without sharing one key. Use the ephemeral service to mint tokens with TTL ~2h and limited scope. That avoids a single long-lived hosted key.
erin: sweet — how do attendees get ephemeral tokens? can I automate that in the workshop lab environment?
jules: yes. You can set up a tiny internal endpoint that mints tokens for authenticated workshop users (we've done this for hackathons). Pattern: attendees authenticate with SSO, your server calls internal ephemeral API, returns token to the browser/session. Make sure tokens are short-lived and scope-limited. Devex docs: https://internal.redwood.devex/ephemeral-tokens and the code sample repo: https://internal.redwood.devex/examples/workshop-ephemeral.
erin: great. one more: if we go with a hosted dev key, can we restrict it by IP so only the workshop VM can use it?
devex-bot: yes, request IP restrictions in the form. Provide the egress IPs for the workshop VMs. We can also set TTL and request an "audit export" for the time window.
tom: practical tip: if any attendee runs into a 429 during workshop, have them switch to the replay mode (we keep a small set of recorded responses) so the flow isn't blocked. Also show them how to check X-RateLimit-Remaining header to see remaining quota.
erin: ok i'll do this: 1) try ephemeral tokens for hands-on 1:1 labs; 2) request a short-lived hosted dev key with IP lock for the central demo; 3) prepare recorded fallbacks. i'll open the request now. thanks everyone :pray:
